newsitem.title: USA: Simpson case gets second jury in two days.
newsitem.headline: Simpson case gets second jury in two days.

text.p: A new jury, the second in two days, was sworn in for the O.J. Simpson civil trial on Friday after one of only two blacks on the original panel was dismissed because of alcohol use.
The reconstituted jury consists of eight whites, one black, one Hispanic, a person of mixed white and Hispanic heritage, and another who is part Asian, part black. There are seven women and five men.

The day started dramatically with a 60-year-old black juror, later identified as Edgar Allen, being dismissed from the original panel sworn in on Thursday. Fellow jurors had complained they smelled alcohol on his breath.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, in dismissing Allen, said: "I conducted an examination yesterday and after having examined five witnesses ... the court has concluded that juror number eight has conducted himself in such a manner with regard to the use of alcohol that he is incapable and unsuitable to serve in this case."
Lawyers for both sides were then allowed to use peremptory challenges -- in which they did not have to give a reason for having a juror excused -- on the remaining panellists.
In less than two hours, the lawyers had a new jury after replacing two of the remaining 11 in addition to Allen.

Simpson, who was found not guilty by a predominantly black jury at a criminal trial last year of murdering his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, is being sued in civil court by the families of the victims.
If found responsible for the murders, the former football star, TV personality and Hollywood actor, could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.
Race played an important part in the criminal trial and is likely to do so in the civil trial. Simpson is black, the murder victims were white.
The juror dismissal was reminiscent of the criminal trial in which two jurors were excused before testimony began and a total of 10 were dismissed for reasons ranging from ill-health to misconduct.

The jurors are known only by their numbers while they are on the panel. Allen, who had been known as juror number eight, was replaced by a white man in his fifties, juror 326, who said he believed police "cover up" for each other.
Simpson's defence team has said it will rely heavily on their theory that evidence in the Simpson case was planted, tampered with and deliberately contaminated.

Juror 215, a white woman in her fifties who previously said she had met Simpson once in a shoe store, was replaced by another white woman in her sixties, juror 400, who said she has strong religious beliefs and thinks that interracial marriages are hard on the children.

A white man in his thirties, juror 427, who said he was not sure about Simpson's guilt or innocence, was replaced by another white man, juror 186, who said he believed some but not all police were corrupt.

Fujisaki cut Friday's proceedings short without explanation before the attorneys began questioning the prospective alternate jurors. The judge wants eight alternates in place before opening statements, scheduled for Wednesday.
Outside the courthouse, Allen, a retired postal worker, told reporters, "I'm an alcoholic, I admit it." Asked what he drank, Allen replied: "Gin, the same thing I'm going to have when I get home."
When reporters asked if he thought he had been kicked off because he was one of only two black jurors, he said: "I don't have any idea if race is a part of this. It might be."
He insisted he felt no racial animosity to anyone involved in the process. "When I look at you," he told one white reporter "I don't see a white man, I see a man."
But Allen said he was not sorry to be forced off the jury. "I've been here since September 18 and I didn't really relish another four months or so (of jury duty)," he said.
